        ### Question
        Before a 60-year-old diabetic patient with stable angina secondary to ischemic heart disease due to subtotal obstruction in the middle third of the anterior descending coronary artery, what treatment would you propose?

        ### Options
        opa. Doctor with vasodilators and beta-blockers to prevent angina.
opb. Expectant with rigorous rest since the decrease in myocardial oxygen demand should decrease angina.
opc. Surgical to revascularize the ischemic myocardium by means of a by-pass of the left mammary artery distal to the lesion in the diseased coronary artery.
opd. Dilation of the coronary artery lesion by means of a therapeutic catheterization.
ope. Therapeutic catheterization to dilate the injury of the diseased artery and implantation of a "stent" in the dilated area.

### Reasoning Chains per Option:
CHAIN: Ischemic heart disease due to subtotal obstruction in the middle third of the anterior descending coronary artery -> Decreased blood flow to the heart muscle -> Angina symptoms. CHAIN: Stable angina -> Increased risk of heart attack -> Requires management to prevent complications. CHAIN: Diabetic patient -> Higher cardiovascular risk -> Requires tailored treatment. CHAIN: Vasodilators and beta-blockers -> Reduce angina symptoms -> Manage stable angina -> 80% CHAIN: Revascularization of the ischemic myocardium -> Improves blood flow to the heart muscle -> Reduces angina symptoms -> 90% CHAIN: Surgical bypass of the left mammary artery distal to the lesion -> Revascularizes the ischemic myocardium -> Improves blood flow -> 85% CHAIN: Therapeutic catheterization to dilate the diseased artery -> Improves blood flow -> May relieve angina symptoms -> 70% CHAIN: Implantation of a stent in the dilated area -> Maintains vessel patency -> Improves blood flow -> 80%
